3: Durarara!! Saika Arc by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is an urban supernatural drama set in Tokyo's Ikebukuro. A string of street slashings has the city on edge, and the attacks seem tied to a cursed blade called Saika that spreads its will to anyone it cuts. Quiet student Anri Sonohara finds herself at the center of it all. It's a good pick for readers who like big ensemble casts and stories where everyone has a secret.
5: One Piece: Ace's Story by Sho Hinata (Viz Media) is an adventure light novel about one of One Piece's most popular characters. At seventeen, Portgas D. Ace sets out to sea alone and begins gathering the crew that becomes the Spade Pirates, including his first mate, Deuce. The story fills in Ace's early days before he joined Whitebeard. It's a great extra for One Piece fans who want more of Ace and his crew.
6: Yokaiden by Nina Matsumoto (Del Rey) is a funny, folklore-filled fantasy adventure. Hamachi is a boy who loves yokai, the spirits and monsters of Japanese legend, even though everyone in his village fears them. When his grandmother dies, he crosses into the yokai world to find the creature he believes is responsible. Fans of quirky monster stories and Japanese folklore will enjoy its humor and lively art.
7: Fairy Tail S by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a collection of short stories from the world of Fairy Tail. Natsu, Lucy, Happy, and the rest of the guild star in standalone tales and bonus chapters, many of them light and comedic. Some stories also fill in moments around the main series. It's a fun extra for fans who already know the characters and want more time with the guild.
11: The Seven Deadly Sins: Seven Days by Nakaba Suzuki (Kodansha) is a fantasy romance spinoff of The Seven Deadly Sins. Long before the main story, the thief Ban sneaks into the Fairy King's Forest in search of the Fountain of Youth. There he meets Elaine, the fairy who guards it, and the two spend seven days together. Fans who want more of Ban and Elaine's story will appreciate this tender side tale.
12: Star Trek: The Manga (Tokyopop) is a science-fiction anthology set in the world of the original Star Trek series. Captain Kirk, Spock, McCoy, and the crew of the Enterprise take on new missions in short stories written and drawn by a mix of creators. Each tale stands on its own, with the exploring spirit of the classic show. It's a nice pick for Trekkies curious to see their favorite crew drawn in manga style.
14: Summer Wars by Mamoru Hosoda (Vertical) is a sci-fi family drama based on the animated film. Shy math whiz Kenji agrees to help his crush, Natsuki, at her great-grandmother's birthday, only to learn she wants him to pose as her fiancé in front of her huge family. Meanwhile, a hacked account throws OZ, the virtual world everyone relies on, into chaos. Readers who like warm family stories with high-tech stakes will enjoy it.
15: Zero's Familiar by Noboru Yamaguchi (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romantic comedy. Louise is a noble student at a magic academy who can't seem to cast a single spell right. When she tries to summon a familiar, she accidentally pulls Saito, an ordinary teenage boy from Japan, into her world. The two bicker constantly as Saito adjusts to life as her servant. It's a good fit for fans of classic magic-school comedies with plenty of romance.
16: Flower in a Storm by Shigeyoshi Takagi (Viz Media) is a lively romantic comedy. Riko Kazama is a high school girl with amazing physical strength who just wants to live a quiet, normal life. That plan falls apart when Ran Tachibana, the bold young heir to a huge company, decides on the spot that she's the girl he'll marry. Readers who like fast-paced, over-the-top romance will have a lot of fun with it.
17: IC in a Sunflower by Mitsukazu Mihara (Tokyopop) is a collection of short stories from the creator of Doll. Its tales explore love, loss, and loneliness, often through people living on the edges of ordinary life, sometimes with a touch of the strange. The mood is quiet and bittersweet. It's a good choice for readers who enjoy thoughtful, gothic-tinged short fiction and Mihara's elegant art.
24: The World's Strongest Rearguard by Towa (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure light novel. After a bus crash, office worker Arihito Atobe wakes up reborn in another world as a Rearguard, a support class that most adventurers overlook. He soon discovers his skills grow powerful when he stands behind his allies, and he begins building a party of his own. Fans of isekai stories about teamwork and leveling up will feel right at home.
25: Gals Can't Be Kind to Otaku!? by Norishiro-chan (Yen Press) is a lighthearted high school romantic comedy. Seo is a quiet otaku who keeps his hobbies to himself, until two popular gyaru classmates take an interest in him. The two girls couldn't be more different, and both keep pulling him into their world. Readers who enjoy sweet, funny school romances will have a good time with it.
26: Devilman by Go Nagai (Seven Seas) is a classic horror action manga. Demons are returning to reclaim the Earth, and Akira Fudo's best friend, Ryo Asuka, believes the only way to fight them is to become one. Gentle Akira merges with the powerful demon Amon, gaining its strength while keeping his human heart. It's a dark, intense story and an important piece of manga history for fans of horror and action.
28: The Tunnel to Summer, the Exit of Goodbyes by Mei Hachimoku (Seven Seas) is a bittersweet romantic drama. High schooler Kaoru Tono hears of a tunnel that will grant your deepest wish, at the cost of years of your life. When he finds it, he discovers new transfer student Anzu Hanashiro wants something from it too. Readers who love quiet, emotional summer stories with a touch of the supernatural will find a lot to like here.
29: Moteki: Love Strikes! by Mitsurou Kubo (Vertical) is a grown-up romantic comedy. Yukiyo Fujimoto is a 29-year-old temp worker who has never had much luck with women. Then, out of nowhere, several women from his past suddenly come back into his life at once, and he has to figure out what he really wants. It's an honest, funny, and sometimes awkward look at dating in your late twenties.
31: Miraculous: Tales of Ladybug and Cat Noir by Thomas Astruc (Kodansha) is a superhero adventure based on the hit animated series. In Paris, teenager Marinette Dupain-Cheng becomes the hero Ladybug, fighting villains alongside her partner, Cat Noir. What neither knows is that Cat Noir is really Adrien, the classmate Marinette has a huge crush on. It's a fun, upbeat pick for kids and fans of the show.
32: Maburaho by Toshihiko Tsukiji (ADV) is a magic-school romantic comedy. Kazuki Shikimori is an ordinary student at an elite magic academy who can only cast a handful of spells in his whole life. When it turns out he comes from a legendary magical bloodline, three very different girls suddenly become determined to win him over. Fans of goofy, fan-service-heavy harem comedies will have fun with it.
33: Sword Art Online: Project Alicization by Reki Kawahara (Yen Press) is a sci-fi fantasy adventure. Kirito wakes up in a forest with no idea how he got there, inside a virtual world so real he can't tell it from reality. There he befriends Eugeo, a young woodcutter, and begins piecing together where he is and why. Fans of Sword Art Online and the Alicization anime will enjoy seeing this arc in manga form.
34: One Thousand and One Nights by Jeon JinSeok and Han SeungHee (Ice Kunion) is a historical drama inspired by the classic tales. The sultan Shahryar, betrayed in the past, marries a new bride each night and has her killed by morning. To save his sister, Sehara disguises himself as a woman and goes to the palace in her place, keeping himself alive by telling the sultan stories. It's a rich, dramatic retelling with beautiful art.
38: The Three-Body Problem: The Comic Edition by Cixin Liu (Yen Press) is a sci-fi thriller adapted from the award-winning novel. Nanomaterials researcher Wang Miao is drawn into an investigation after a wave of scientists die mysteriously, and he begins seeing a strange countdown that no one else can see. His search leads him to a puzzling virtual reality game. Readers who like big ideas and hard science fiction will find a lot to think about.
39: The Concierge at Hokkyoku Department Store by Tsuchika Nishimura (Seven Seas) is a gentle workplace story with a touch of fantasy. Akino is a new concierge in training at a grand department store whose customers are animals, many of them extinct species. She works hard to help each guest find exactly what they need, despite her nervous mistakes. It's a sweet, thoughtful read for anyone who enjoys cozy stories with a little melancholy.
40: Hyde and Closer by Haro Aso (Viz Media) is a supernatural action comedy. Shunpei Closer is a timid boy whose sorcerer grandfather sends him a teddy bear named Hyde. Hyde turns out to be a tough, foul-mouthed fighter sworn to protect him, and he arrives just as sorcerers start coming after Shunpei. It's a fun, fast-paced pick for readers who like quirky magic battles and odd-couple heroes.
44: Boruto: Two Blue Vortex by Masashi Kishimoto (Viz Media) is a ninja action story that picks up the Boruto saga after a time skip. Boruto Uzumaki has been away from the Hidden Leaf Village, branded a fugitive while the people closest to him have been turned against him. Now older and stronger, he returns to face the dangers threatening his home. Fans of Naruto and Boruto will want to follow this next chapter.
55: Weathering with You by Makoto Shinkai (Vertical) is a romantic fantasy based on the animated film. High schooler Hodaka runs away from his island home to Tokyo, where it rains day after day. Struggling to get by, he meets Hina, a cheerful girl who can make the sky clear just by praying. Readers who loved Your Name or enjoy bittersweet stories about young love will find it lovely.
57: Bungo Stray Dogs: Beast by Kafka Asagiri (Yen Press) is an alternate-universe action spinoff of Bungo Stray Dogs. In this world, the roles are reversed: Ryunosuke Akutagawa works for the Armed Detective Agency, while Atsushi Nakajima is a deadly member of the Port Mafia. Behind it all, Dazai is pulling the strings. Fans of the main series will enjoy seeing familiar characters in a darker, flipped story.
61: Orochi by Kazuo Umezz (Viz Media) is a classic horror anthology. Orochi is a mysterious, ageless girl with strange powers who drifts from place to place, quietly watching the lives of the families she meets. Each story uncovers the jealousy, fear, and cruelty hidden in ordinary homes. It's a great pick for horror fans who want unsettling, old-school tales from a master of the genre.
65: Butterflies, Flowers by Yuki Yoshihara (Viz Media) is a workplace romantic comedy for older teens. Choko Kuze's family was once wealthy, but now she's an ordinary office temp. Her strict, demanding boss turns out to be Masayuki Domoto, the servant boy who looked after her when she was little, and he still calls her "milady" when they're alone. Readers who enjoy funny, slightly steamy office romances will have fun with it.
72: The Ring by Koji Suzuki (Dark Horse) is a horror mystery based on the famous novel. Journalist Kazuyuki Asakawa starts digging into the sudden deaths of four teenagers who died at the same moment. His search leads him to a mysterious videotape that is said to kill anyone who watches it within a week. Fans of classic Japanese horror will enjoy this chilling version of the story.
73: Bloom into You Anthology (Seven Seas) is a collection of short stories celebrating Nio Nakatani's yuri romance Bloom into You. Different artists offer their own takes on Yuu, Touko, and the rest of the student council, with stories that range from sweet to funny. It's a nice extra for fans of the main series who want to spend more time with these characters.
79: Kingyo Used Books by Seimu Yoshizaki (Viz Media) is a warm slice-of-life story about the love of manga. Kingyo is a cozy secondhand manga shop, and each chapter follows a different customer who comes in looking for a book. Along the way, readers discover classic manga and the memories tied to them. It's a perfect pick for manga fans who love old books and the stories behind them.
82: Gal Gohan by Marii Taiyou (Seven Seas) is a comedy about food and friendship. Miku Okazaki is a cheerful gyaru who isn't great at school, so she joins the cooking club to earn extra credit. The club's only adviser is Shinji Yamato, a straight-laced teacher who now has to teach her to cook. Readers who enjoy cooking manga and odd-couple comedies will find plenty of fun here.
88: Kuma Miko by Masume Yoshimoto (One Peace Books) is a gentle countryside comedy. Machi is a young shrine maiden living in a remote mountain village, where her best friend and guardian is Natsu, a talking bear. Machi dreams of going to high school in the big city, but Natsu worries she isn't ready. It's a sweet, funny read for fans of slice-of-life stories with a cute animal sidekick.
89: Frau Faust by Kore Yamazaki (Kodansha) is a dark fantasy adventure from the creator of The Ancient Magus' Bride. Marion, a young boy, crosses paths with Johanna Faust, a mysterious woman who claims to be the legendary Doctor Faust. She is searching for the scattered pieces of the demon Mephistopheles, and Marion decides to follow her. Readers who like quiet, magical stories with a touch of mystery will enjoy it.
90: Deltora Quest by Emily Rodda (Kodansha) is a fantasy adventure based on the popular children's book series. The kingdom of Deltora has fallen under the rule of the evil Shadow Lord, and the seven gems of the magical Belt of Deltora have been scattered. Young Lief sets out with his companions to find them and free the land. It's a fun, classic quest story for kids and fans of the original books.
94: Les Misérables (Manga Classics) by Crystal S. Chan (Udon Entertainment) is a faithful manga adaptation of Victor Hugo's classic novel. Jean Valjean is released after nineteen years in prison for stealing bread, but he can't escape his past or the relentless Inspector Javert. A single act of kindness sets him on a new path. It's a great way for students and new readers to experience the story.
98: Sword of the Demon Hunter: Kijin Gentosho by Motoo Nakanishi (Seven Seas) is a historical fantasy light novel. In Edo-period Japan, Jinta is the guardian of a shrine maiden in a small mountain village, sworn to protect her from demons. A fateful encounter in the forest sets him on a path that will stretch across centuries. Readers who like sweeping, thoughtful stories about time and fate will find a lot to love.
100: Do You Love Your Mom and Her Two-Hit Multi-Target Attacks? by Dachima Inaka (Yen Press) is a fantasy comedy. Teenager Masato is thrilled to be chosen to test a new online game, until he finds out his mom, Mamako, is coming along. Worse, she turns out to be ridiculously overpowered and steals the spotlight in every battle. It's a goofy, warm pick for readers who enjoy isekai parodies and family humor.
103: Code:Breaker by Akimine Kamijyo (Del Rey) is a supernatural action series. High schooler Sakura Sakurakoji witnesses a boy burning criminals to ashes with blue flames, and no trace is left behind. The next day, that same boy, Rei Ogami, transfers into her class. Sakura becomes determined to understand who he is and stop him. Fans of dark, fast-paced action and vigilante stories will enjoy it.
108: After Hours by Yuhta Nishio (Viz Media) is a grown-up romance set in Tokyo's nightlife. Emi is a young woman who feels a little lost until she meets Kei, a confident DJ, at a club. Kei pulls her into the world of music and late nights, and the two grow close. It's a short, heartfelt story for readers who enjoy realistic romance between women and the energy of club culture.
110: Clamp School Defenders Duklyon by CLAMP (Dark Horse) is a comedy that pokes fun at classic sentai hero shows. Kentaro and Takeshi are two students at the enormous Clamp School who are secretly the heroes Duklyon. They fight a strange villainous organization that keeps attacking the campus, usually with ridiculous schemes. Fans of CLAMP and goofy superhero parodies will have a good laugh.
112: unOrdinary by uru-chan (Harper Alley) is a superhero drama based on the popular webcomic. In a world where almost everyone has powers, John is a high school student with none, and he's stuck at the bottom of his school's strict power-based ranking. He keeps his head down and tries not to cause trouble, but there's more to him than anyone knows. It's a great pick for readers who like stories about bullying, power, and hidden strength.
114: Satoko and Nada by Yupechika (Seven Seas) is a warm slice-of-life comedy about friendship across cultures. Satoko is a Japanese student studying abroad in America, and her new roommate is Nada, a Muslim woman from Saudi Arabia. Through short, funny chapters, the two share food, traditions, and everyday surprises. It's a kind, thoughtful read for anyone who enjoys gentle stories about learning from each other.
117: Liselotte and Witch's Forest by Natsuki Takaya (Viz Media) is a fantasy story from the creator of Fruits Basket. Liselotte, a young noblewoman, has been sent to live at the edge of the world, near a forest said to be home to witches. With her two loyal servants, Anna and Engetsu, she tries to make a new life there, but she carries a sad secret from her past. Readers who enjoy gentle, emotional fantasy will like it.
121: Napping Princess by Kenji Kamiyama (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure based on the animated film. High school student Kokone Morikawa loves to nap, and she keeps having strange dreams about a princess in a kingdom full of machines. When her father is suddenly arrested, she realizes her dreams may hold the key to helping him. Readers who like stories that blend dreams and reality will enjoy it.
125: Durarara!! SH by Ryohgo Narita (Yen Press) is an urban mystery light novel that continues the Durarara!! story. Two years after the events of the original series, a new group of students arrives in Ikebukuro, a neighborhood still full of strange people and urban legends. As fresh mysteries unfold, they cross paths with familiar faces. Fans of Durarara!! who want more of its colorful cast will enjoy this sequel.
131: Onegai Twins by Akikan (Dr. Master) is a romantic comedy based on the anime. Maiku Kamishiro lives alone and works from home, and all he knows about his family is an old photo of himself with a sister. Then two girls, Miina and Karen, show up at his door, each claiming to be the sister in the picture. Fans of the anime and lighthearted mixed-up family comedies will enjoy it.
132: Avril Lavigne's Make 5 Wishes by Camilla d'Errico (Del Rey) is a supernatural drama inspired by Avril Lavigne. Hana is a shy, lonely girl who wishes she could fit in. When she meets Neddy, a strange creature who can grant her wishes, her life starts to change, but each wish comes at a cost. It's a quick, moody read for fans of Avril and stories about growing up and believing in yourself.
133: Guru Guru Pon-chan by Satomi Ikezawa (Del Rey) is a romantic comedy with a dog's-eye twist. Ponta is a lively Labrador puppy who finds a magic bone that turns her into a human girl. Now she can follow the boy she has a crush on, but she still has a lot to learn about being a person. Readers who like silly, sweet romances and animal fans will enjoy it.
140: Neon Genesis Evangelion: The Shinji Ikari Raising Project by Osamu Takahashi (Dark Horse) is a school romantic comedy set in an alternate version of Evangelion. In this world, there's no war with Angels; Shinji is a regular student, Asuka is his bossy childhood friend and neighbor, and Rei is the new transfer student. It's a lighthearted take for Evangelion fans who'd like to see the characters live happier lives.
141: Monster by Naoki Urasawa (Viz Media) is a psychological thriller. Dr. Kenzo Tenma is a brilliant surgeon in Germany who chooses to save a young boy's life instead of a powerful politician's, risking his career. Years later, a string of murders makes Tenma realize the boy he saved may have grown up to be a monster. Readers who love suspenseful, character-driven mysteries will find it hard to put down.
144: Summertime Rendering by Yasuki Tanaka (Udon) is a supernatural mystery thriller. Shinpei returns to his small island hometown for the funeral of Ushio, his childhood friend, who drowned while saving a little girl. But rumors of mysterious shadows that take the place of people suggest her death may not have been an accident. Fans of time-loop mysteries and creepy summer stories will be hooked.
145: Tenjo Tenge by Oh! Great (Viz Media) is a martial arts action series. Souichiro Nagi and his friend Bob Makihara transfer to Todou Academy, planning to take over the school by force. Instead, they run into the Juken Club, a group of fighters with far more skill than they expected. It's a fight-heavy story with lots of fan service, best for older readers who like intense martial arts battles.
148: Genkaku Picasso by Usamaru Furuya (Viz Media) is a supernatural school story. Hikari "Picasso" Hamura is a quiet art lover who survives a terrible accident, but his friend Chiaki doesn't. Now Chiaki's ghost tells him he must use his drawings to help troubled people, by drawing what's in their hearts and stepping inside. It's an odd, touching read for fans of emotional stories with a creative twist.
149: Digimon Zero Two by Akiyoshi Hongo (Tokyopop) is a monster adventure based on the second Digimon anime. A few years after the first DigiDestined saved the Digital World, a new group of kids, led by hot-headed Davis, receive Digivices of their own. They partner with new Digimon to stop the Digimon Emperor. It's a fun, nostalgic pick for kids and longtime Digimon fans.
153: Get Backers by Yuya Aoki (Tokyopop) is a supernatural action series. Ban Mido and Ginji Amano are the Get Backers, a pair of retrieval agents who promise to recover anything that has been lost or stolen, for a price. Ban has a mysterious Evil Eye, and Ginji can generate electricity. Fans of action-packed stories with odd-couple partners and a lot of humor will enjoy it.
154: Hotel Africa by Hee Jung Park (Tokyopop) is a quiet, reflective drama. Elvis grew up at Hotel Africa, a small motel in the Utah desert run by his mother and grandfather. Looking back on his childhood, he remembers the travelers who passed through and the ways they touched his family's lives. It's a gentle, heartfelt story for readers who enjoy thoughtful slice-of-life tales about family and belonging.
162: Kujibiki Unbalance by Kio Shimoku (Del Rey) is a school comedy spun off from Genshiken. Chihiro Enomoto starts at a school where everything, even who leads the student council, is decided by lottery. To his shock, he's drawn as the new student council president, alongside his childhood friend Tokino. Fans of Genshiken and goofy school comedies will have fun with it.
164: Densha Otoko by Hitori Nakano (CMX) is a gentle romantic comedy based on the famous true story. A shy otaku stands up to a drunk harassing a woman on a train. Afterward, she sends him a thank-you gift, and, with no idea what to do next, he turns to an online forum where strangers help him find the courage to see her again. It's a sweet, feel-good read for anyone who's ever felt awkward in love.
165: Eagle: The Making of an Asian-American President by Kaiji Kawaguchi (Viz Media) is a political drama. Japanese-American senator Kenneth Yamaoka is running for president of the United States. Takashi Jo, a young reporter from Japan, is asked to cover his campaign and soon learns he is Yamaoka's son. Readers who enjoy political thrillers and stories about family and ambition will find it gripping.
172: Alien Nine by Hitoshi Tomizawa (CPM) is a sci-fi drama with a dark edge. Sixth-grader Yuri Otani is chosen against her will to join her school's Alien Party, a group of students tasked with capturing the aliens that keep showing up on campus. To fight them, she has to wear a strange creature called a Borg on her head. It's a strange, unsettling read for fans of offbeat science fiction.
176: Return to Labyrinth by Jake T. Forbes (Tokyopop) is a fantasy sequel to Jim Henson's film Labyrinth. Years after his sister Sarah rescued him, Toby is now a teenager who feels overlooked and ordinary. Then Jareth, the Goblin King, brings him back to the Labyrinth with plans for his future. Fans of the movie will enjoy this continuation of its strange and magical world.
181: Codename: Sailor V by Naoko Takeuchi (Kodansha) is a magical girl adventure and the series that came before Sailor Moon. Minako Aino is a cheerful eighth grader who loves video games and cute boys. When a talking white cat named Artemis gives her a magic pen, she becomes the mysterious hero Sailor V and fights the villains threatening Tokyo. Sailor Moon fans will love seeing where it all began.
183: Fairy Tail: Blue Mistral by Hiro Mashima (Kodansha) is a fantasy spinoff starring Wendy Marvell. The young sky dragon slayer has just joined the Fairy Tail guild along with her cat partner, Carla. As she settles in, she takes on jobs, makes new friends, and works to grow stronger. It's a cute, lighthearted extra for Fairy Tail fans and younger readers.
186: Neko Ramen by Kenji Sonishi (Tokyopop) is a gag comedy about a very unusual restaurant. Taisho is a cat who runs his own ramen shop and is determined to make it a success. Unfortunately, his cooking ideas are usually bizarre, and his only regular customer is a patient salaryman. Short, silly chapters make it a great pick for cat lovers and anyone who enjoys quirky comedy.
189: Pichi Pichi Pitch: Mermaid Melody by Pink Hanamori and Michiko Yokote (Del Rey) is a magical girl romance. Lucia is a mermaid princess who comes to land to find the pearl she gave to a human boy years ago. She meets Kaito, a surfer who might be that boy, but if she tells him who she really is, she'll turn into sea foam. Fans of magical girl stories and sweet romance will enjoy it.
190: Pretty Boy Detective Club by NISIOISIN (Vertical) is a mystery comedy. Mayumi Dojima has spent ten years searching for a star she once saw in the sky. When she brings her case to the Pretty Boy Detective Club, a group of eccentric and stylish boys who solve mysteries their own way, they agree to help. Readers who like witty, quirky mysteries will find it charming.
192: She Likes Gays But Not Me by Akira Hirahara (Yen Press) is a coming-of-age drama. Jun Ando is a high school boy who is secretly gay and dating an older man. When he runs into his classmate Sae Miura buying boys' love manga, she has no idea he's gay, and the two start a friendship. It's a thoughtful, honest read for older teens and adults who enjoy stories about identity and belonging.
